title: Shadow traffic: retention defaults + prompt/response redaction pipeline
author: Kevin Osei
description: Context: Shadow Traffic generates additional artifacts (request/response pairs + scoring payload references). We need strict data minimization by default and deterministic redaction so we can store enough to compute quality deltas while meeting Dedicated/Private constraints. This PR implements (1) retention defaults by deployment mode, (2) a redaction/transform pipeline for shadow artifacts, and (3) configuration toggles + audit-friendly metadata to support regulated customers. Summary of changes: - Adds `shadow_artifact_retention` config with safe defaults (Hosted: 24h; Dedicated: 7d; Private: 0h unless explicitly configured) and per-tenant overrides with validation. - Introduces `ShadowArtifactRedactor` (server-side) that transforms prompts/inputs and outputs before persistence: structured allowlist, truncation, hashing of identifiers, and regex-based PII scrubbing. - Adds storage layout for artifacts with TTL enforcement (DB TTL where supported + object-store lifecycle rules) and a periodic GC job for backends without native TTL. - Adds knobs for Dedicated/Private: `retention_hours`, `store_raw_prompts` (default false), `store_raw_responses` (default false), `redaction_profile` (standard|strict), and `export_audit_metadata` for SIEM export. - Updates ingestion to persist only redacted payloads; raw payloads never leave the request handler boundary (fail-closed for raw capture, fail-open for shadowing overall). - Adds metrics + logs for redaction effectiveness and retention GC: `shadow.redaction.actions_total`, `shadow.redaction.bytes_dropped`, `shadow.retention.gc.deleted_total`, and `shadow.retention.gc.lag_seconds`. - Docs in code comments reference Confluence: Security & Compliance > Shadow traffic data retention and redaction (v1). Behavior details: - Redaction is applied prior to enqueueing scoring payload references; scoring workers fetch only redacted text blobs. - Prompt redaction uses a best-effort regex pass (email/phone/SSN-like patterns) plus an allowlist for structured inputs (`messages[].role`, `messages[].content`); everything else is dropped unless explicitly allowed. - Content truncation defaults: prompts 8KB, responses 16KB (post-redaction), configurable only for Dedicated/Private with max caps enforced. - Stable hashing uses HMAC-SHA256 with a per-tenant key (KMS-managed) for `user_id`, `session_id`, and request fingerprints so customers can correlate within their tenant without exposing raw values. - Retention is enforced on both the artifact table and associated blob objects; deletion is idempotent and safe to re-run. Risk/mitigations: - Cardinality: we do not emit raw identifiers in metrics; only redaction action counts and coarse-grained profiles. - Performance: redaction runs in the async persistence path; synchronous request path only copies required fields into an internal buffer and immediately drops raw references after redaction. - Private deployments: when object-store lifecycle rules are unavailable, the GC job is mandatory and will run as part of the telemetry stack; documented in release notes for Private packaging. Testing: - Unit tests for allowlist behavior, regex scrubber, truncation, and hashing determinism. - Integration test that verifies raw prompts are not persisted when `store_raw_prompts=false`. - Migration test for existing shadow artifact rows (backfill redaction on read is NOT supported; this PR gates storage behind the feature flag so we don’t create mixed-mode tables). Rollout: gated behind `shadow_artifacts_persist_redacted_v1` (default off). Dedicated/Private can override via control plane config. Follow-ups: - Implement customer-configurable field-level allowlists for JSON tool inputs (deferred; requires product + security review). - Add UI surfacing of retention profile in Console (tracked in ENG-5408).

conversation: Marcus Lin (Security) [review]: Can we confirm raw prompts never get written to disk when `store_raw_prompts=false`? Also please document the regex patterns used and the known limitations (false positives/negatives) so we don’t oversell this as "PII safe". Kevin Osei (author): Confirmed: raw prompts are only held in-memory in the handler scope; we construct a redacted payload and only that crosses into the persistence layer. Added an integration test (`noRawPromptPersistence.test.ts`) that asserts the DB row + blob contain only redacted content and the raw buffer is dropped. I also added a comment block in `ShadowArtifactRedactor.ts` describing the regex set + limitations. Naomi Feldman (Compliance) [review]: Private default retention should be 0 unless explicitly set. Dedicated default 7d is fine but ensure max cap exists to prevent "accidental 90d" configs without approval. Kevin: Updated defaults: Private=0h (disabled). Added validation caps: Hosted max 72h; Dedicated/Private max 30d unless `compliance_override=true` (control plane-only, not exposed in Console). Logan Wright (Telemetry) [review]: Please ensure no high-cardinality tags are emitted. The metric names look fine; can we remove `tenant_id` from the structured log? Kevin: Removed `tenant_id` from info logs; kept it only in restricted audit logs (RBAC-protected) and as a hashed `tenant_key` for correlation. Nadia Rahman (Pipelines) [review]: GC job: what happens if it falls behind? We need a metric and an alert hook. Kevin: Added `shadow.retention.gc.lag_seconds` and `shadow.retention.gc.last_success_timestamp`. SRE can alert on lag > 6h for Dedicated and > 24h for Private. Sean Gallagher (SRE) [review]: Fail-open requirement: ensure redaction failure does not impact user response; but we should fail-closed for artifact persistence (don’t persist raw). Kevin: Implemented: if redaction throws, we drop the artifact and increment `shadow.redaction.failures_total`. Shadow routing remains unaffected. Benji Okafor (Control plane) [review]: Please align naming with other policy objects (`*_hours`, `*_enabled`). Kevin: Renamed fields to `retention_hours` and `persist_artifacts_enabled`; added migration alias handling for the earlier draft fields. Approvals: Marcus Lin approved after changes. Naomi Feldman approved. Logan/Nadia approved. Sean approved with note to wire alert rules in follow-up (ENG-5409). Merged after CI green.
release_notes: Shadow traffic artifacts are now stored redacted by default with strict retention defaults (Hosted 24h; Dedicated 7d; Private disabled unless configured). Dedicated/Private deployments can configure retention and redaction profiles via control plane values. Adds GC job for environments without native TTL and new metrics to monitor retention enforcement and redaction behavior.
